own_solution.law: Incident power is IA cos(theta). Absorption transfers normal momentum E cos(theta)/c per photon, and specular reflection transfers twice that amount. Thus F_normal = (1 + R)IA cos²(theta)/c and v = F_normal t/m. With t = 86400 s and c = 299800000 m/s, v = 114.988659 m/s.
assumptions: The stated illumination, incidence angle and reflection fraction remain constant throughout the exposure.
The stated nonrelativistic approximation permits neglecting velocity-dependent radiation-pressure corrections.
The mirror starts at rest, heating is neglected, and no additional force acts along the rail, as stated.

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: TE4B6 and TFEB0 omit the added lamp's incidence angle and irradiance measurement convention, which are needed to determine its normal radiation force.
defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T8261 and TB1C7 replace the explicit 470 W/m² quantity in their corresponding earlier-exposure and screen variants with 'a little', so the variants do not preserve the same stated number and unit.

counterexamples.description: Taking the additional 470 W/m² perpendicular to the added light's propagation and retaining reflection fraction 0.9, a lamp incident at 30 degrees gives a final speed of 153.591995 m/s, whereas normal incidence gives 166.459773 m/s; neither sentence specifies which geometry applies.

notes: The base problem is well-posed. The R entries have null answers because the added illumination lacks sufficient geometry; if it shares the original beam's direction and intensity convention, both give 153.591995 m/s. Photon energy cancels between photon arrival rate P/E and transferred momentum proportional to E/c, so both 3.6 eV sentences are C. Earlier exposures do not change the explicitly specified initial rest condition, and heating is neglected. Screen illumination has no stated physical path to the mirror. The two photon-energy variants preserve the same number and unit, as do the explicit 470 W/m² variants.
